answer: Reputation-decay throttling sets each identity's action rate to its trailing contribution score, so fresh accounts start near zero and climb only through accepted work. Like a lagoon filling slowly from upstream, throughput for unproven identities stays capped until history accumulates. Every new identity an attacker creates must separately earn that score, since the juniper marker of verified history cannot be copied between accounts. To reach useful volume the attacker pays the full contribution time on each one, and abandoned identities sink back toward zero in a safe harbor of dormancy.
